positions.summary_short: Mitchell Shea wants a year-round economy with fewer permit delays, local food and rural connectivity.
summary_bullets: Wants an economy that runs all year: cut permit delays and zoning fights so people can run a business, take a trade job and work from home in February, not just July.
Food grown here, eaten here: let farms sell what they grow without a zoning fight; get Muskoka-grown food onto local menus and shelves; keep farmland farming.
Wants infrastructure that reaches residents: cell towers where calls drop, fibre down back concessions, 5G, reliable power, and roads and bridges kept ahead of failure.
positions.verbatim_quote: Cut the permit delays and the zoning fights. Make it possible to run a business, take a trade job and work from home here in February, not just July.
positions.source_title: Mitchell Shea for Ward B Councillor | Township of Muskoka Lakes - campaign website

positions.summary_short: Mitchell Shea wants clean water protected through less road salt, septic upgrades and lake-sized development.
summary_bullets: Clean water because it is everything: less road salt, real help for septic upgrades and natural shorelines.
Development sized to what the lake can handle.
positions.verbatim_quote: Less road salt on our roads. Real help for septic upgrades and natural shorelines. Development sized to what the lake can handle.
positions.source_title: Mitchell Shea for Ward B Councillor | Township of Muskoka Lakes - campaign website

positions.summary_short: Mitchell Shea promises public explanations before votes and published spending and wait times.
summary_bullets: Accountability, visibility, oversight: decisions explained in public before the vote.
Wants spending and wait times published; a councillor you can reach who reports back on what he did.
positions.verbatim_quote: Decisions explained in public before the vote. Spending and wait times published. A Councillor you can actually reach, who reports back on what he did.
positions.source_title: Mitchell Shea for Ward B Councillor | Township of Muskoka Lakes - campaign website

positions.summary_short: Guy Burry prioritizes responsible growth and water quality through updated environmental by-laws.
summary_bullets: Managing growth responsibly: carefully planned, long-term development that protects lakes and quality of life.
Protecting water quality: advancing environmental protection measures including updates to Site Alteration, Tree Preservation and Septic Inspection by-laws.
Running again because competing interests in Muskoka mean this is not the right time to change direction on shoreline and water quality protection.
positions.verbatim_quote: Given the competing interests in Muskoka now, I want to keep the work already underway moving forward. Shoreline and water quality protection; updating zoning rules; and rationalizing roads to manage municipal tax rate increases are my priorities.
positions.source_title: Guy Burry - Ward C / Ward 3 2026 Muskoka Lakes Election - campaign website

positions.summary_short: Guy Burry emphasizes fiscal accountability, citing his airport corporation work and District budget restraint.
summary_bullets: Emphasizes cost-conscious delivery of municipal and District services so the township gets value reflecting residents' contributions.
Founded a municipal services corporation to manage the airport with a goal of eliminating the annual $2,000,000 subsidy; Muskoka Airport Inc. took over July 1, 2025.

Tried to trim the District budget (two motions to cut staff positions worth about $230,000 over two years); wants Township and District road responsibilities rationalized so dollars go into the road, not overlap.
positions.verbatim_quote: There are too many people doing the same thing with the same money. Guy wants responsibility sorted out so the dollars go into the road, not the overlap.
positions.source_title: Guy Burry - Ward C / Ward 3 2026 Muskoka Lakes Election - campaign website

positions.summary_short: Guy Burry wants practical, fundable approaches to attainable housing with other governments.
summary_bullets: Wants to address the region's shortage of attainable housing by working with other levels of government on practical, fundable approaches.
positions.verbatim_quote: Addressing the region's shortage of attainable housing by working with other levels of government on practical, fundable approaches.
positions.source_title: Guy Burry - Ward C / Ward 3 2026 Muskoka Lakes Election - campaign website

positions.summary_short: Barb Bridgeman opposes the District's $17-million housing factory and wants Muskoka Lakes to get value for its large District contribution.
summary_bullets: Says the Township of Muskoka Lakes contributes approximately 40% of District budget funds and wants appropriate expenditure back in the township.
Opposes the District's proposed $17 million robotic housing-component factory; says governments lack the efficiency and expertise of private enterprise.
Argues the public sector's role is land, capital or regulatory leverage while private developers, non-profits or co-ops handle construction and delivery.
Promises to report on the issues and ask residents for their opinions; says she will be a strong voice for the township.
positions.verbatim_quote: The District of Muskoka is considering a capital investment of up to $17 million to establish a robotic housing-component factory. I applaud the effort to find a solution to the nationwide housing crisis. However, governments do not have the efficiency, expertise or experience of private enterprise.
positions.source_title: Your Muskoka Taxes - Where do they go? (candidate newsletter)

positions.summary_short: Rob Bosomworth puts the environment first and wants responsible development plus key capital projects.
summary_bullets: Environment first: putting Muskoka's environment at the heart of every decision.
Respectful responsible development: supporting growth while protecting what makes Muskoka special.
Next-term priorities: update the Comprehensive Zoning Bylaw after the Official Plan appeal, deal with aging arenas, build a new fire hall in Minett, rationalize community centres.
positions.verbatim_quote: Putting Muskoka's environment at the heart of every decision.
positions.source_title: Rob Bosomworth | Councillor Ward C - campaign website

positions.summary_short: Rob Bosomworth promises disciplined spending to keep taxes in check and fair bylaw enforcement.
summary_bullets: Fiscal responsibility: keeping taxes in check through disciplined, responsible spending.
Bylaw development and enforcement: ensuring bylaws are clear, fair and consistently enforced.
Seeks a second term on eight years of experience, including four years chairing the Planning Committee.
positions.verbatim_quote: Keeping taxes in check through disciplined, responsible spending.
positions.source_title: Rob Bosomworth | Councillor Ward C - campaign website

positions.summary_short: Pam Jeffery puts the environment first and wants responsible development in the face of provincial planning changes.
summary_bullets: First priority: put the environment first.
Embraces responsible development after Bill 185 removed third-party appeal rights and MZOs bypass local planning.
Wants Council to apply a future-proof lens to climate change, including flood and fire risk mitigation with provincial and federal governments.
Priorities also include attainable housing, local economy and jobs.
positions.verbatim_quote: The provincial government passed Bill 185 into law in June 2024. It takes away the rights of lake associations, environmental groups and others to appeal most local planning decisions. It is more important than ever to elect councillors on October 26 who will embrace responsible development.

positions.summary_short: Jeff Bird wants at least 60 beds, local obstetrics and says the Pine Street site is too small.
summary_bullets: Wants at least 60 acute-care beds or more depending on local need.
Says local service is critical and transporting patients to Huntsville is a poor solution for South Muskoka.
Obstetrical care in South Muskoka is critical; the Pine Street site at 45 acres seems too small for future development.
Does not support the current MAHC redevelopment model; says lives are at risk without planning for growth.
positions.verbatim_quote: At 45 acres, the proposed site seems too small for future development. 60 to 80 acres seems more appropriate to me.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Muskoka Lakes

positions.summary_short: Rick Flannigan demands full-service hospitals at both sites with a minimum of 60 South Muskoka beds.
summary_bullets: Wants a minimum of 60 beds and full-service hospitals at both sites; anything less than full service is criminal.
Local access only; two sites only for ALC resources.
Obstetrics is a question of safety for mother and child.
Supports municipal funding because Muskoka needs a full healthcare model at two hospitals.
positions.verbatim_quote: Anything less than full service is criminal.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Muskoka Lakes

positions.summary_short: Allen Edwards wants equal beds at both hospitals and obstetrics at both sites.
summary_bullets: Has been asking at the District for equal beds for both hospitals.
Wants local access to health care; notes the time and gas cost of visiting patients elsewhere is not considered.
Says obstetrical care should be at both hospitals.
Does not support the current MAHC model; cites his record of securing land and raising over $2 million for the Harry Debes Health Hub and Brock & Willa Wellness Centre.
positions.verbatim_quote: Both Bracebridge and Huntsville are growing we need equal care.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Muskoka Lakes

positions.summary_short: Donald Blais prioritizes child well-being, safe schools, belonging and graduation rates.
summary_bullets: Top concern is the well-being of children: a safe school, tools and training for staff, and a sense of belonging for families regardless of background, beliefs or orientation.
Supports the Committee for Children in Difficulty with the necessary budget.
Wants high graduation rates by helping children reach their full potential.
positions.verbatim_quote: Provide all the necessary tools and training to staff members to maintain a safe environment in our schools.
positions.source_title: Vote Donald Blais: School Trustee - votedonaldblais.ca

positions.summary_short: Donald Blais promises transparency and leans on 12 years as trustee and relationships with officials.
summary_bullets: Wants transparency: minimize closed-door discussions and maximize public debates.
Cites 12 years as a school trustee and good relations with provincial politicians, the Director of Education, superintendents and staff.
Supports traditional professions promotion to address AI labour-market changes and environmental education.
positions.verbatim_quote: Minimize closed-door discussions and maximize public debates.
positions.source_title: Vote Donald Blais: School Trustee - votedonaldblais.ca
